extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and consumers of wartime news
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and dispatches covering military operations, civil defense, and related human-interest scenes during wartime (WWII-era newspaper coverage). Emphasizes use of official communiqués, factual observation, and navigation of censorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality of reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: "The wartime nations demand reporters be impartial."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should present facts without taking sides; 'tell what they see and what they can justify as facts.' Avoid partisan framing in wartime dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withhold military information useful to the enemy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Nearly all countries bar what they consider military information that might be useful to an enemy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publish details of troop movements, lines of communication, shipping histories, or other operational information that could aid the enemy; expect and comply with censorship prohibitions on such material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance truth-telling with censorship compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Passage warns that obeyed fear and passive acceptance of censorship 'would stifle much truth' but also notes reporters operate under censorship constraints and risk expulsion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue and publish verifiable, vital truths where possible while recognizing legal and safety limits imposed by wartime censorship and the risk of being expelled or otherwise restricted by authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use authoritative official sources (communiqués) for operational detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The text reproduces and relies on Air Ministry communiqués giving port-by-port accounts of bombing raids and official damage assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting military operations, cite official communiqués and government sources for operational claims and detailed accounts; these provide authoritative, attributable information for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground reports in verifiable observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters are 'told to tell what they see and what they can justify as facts.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor first-hand observation and verifiable facts over rumor or inference; clearly distinguish confirmed facts from conjecture in copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use human-interest and descriptive detail to convey atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: News items illustrate scenes (Roosevelt inspecting shipyards, patients in wheelchairs greeting him, workers cheering; vivid desert descriptions of troops marching and water shortages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concrete, human-scale details and sensory description to convey the atmosphere and human impact of military and political events, helping readers grasp the stakes and emotions involved.
